claim: The Calanques are the headline thing to do in Cassis, with ~20km of waymarked footpaths linking Marseille to Cassis and signature experiences like sunrise at En-Vau and swimming at Port-Pin.
quote: The Calanques link Marseille to Cassis along almost 20km of waymarked footpaths. ... Hiking at sunrise in En-Vau, sunset on the Route des Crêtes, swimming in the turquoise waters of Port-Pin.

claim: The park entrance near the Cassis peninsula/Port-Miou is 30 minutes on foot from Cassis town centre; Port-Pin is a further 15 minutes and En-Vau a further 30 minutes, with a steep climb to En-Vau.
quote: just 30 minutes on foot from Cassis town centre ... The Port-Pin calanque is a further 15 minutes, and En-Vau calanque a further 30 minutes ... the climb to En-Vau calanque is steep and can be difficult, particularly in summer.

claim: From Port-Miou it is 2.3 km (30 min) to Port-Pin and 3.8 km (1h15) to En-Vau; the trail is easy to Port-Pin and medium to En-Vau, with slippery rocks on the old seaside GR and a hands-on descent into En-Vau.
quote: To Port Pin: 2,3km (30min) ... To En-vau: 3,8km (1h15) ... Easy until Port Pin / Medium for En-vau ... rocks that are extremely slippery on the part on the sea side in the old GR ... don't hesitate to use your hands.

claim: The classic route starts from Port-Miou on the Cassis peninsula and follows the GR51/98 trail marked in red and white, taking about 1h30 to 2h one way.
quote: The most popular route starts from Port-Miou cove (Cassis peninsula) and follows the GR51/98 trail marked in red and white, taking 1h30 to 2h one way.

claim: The Presqu'île parking sits above Port-Miou (1 Avenue Plage Bleue, 13260 Cassis), free off-season and ~8 euros in high season; the free Gorguettes lot (220 spaces) is a ~30 min walk or served by a free shuttle to Cassis centre and Port-Miou.
quote: The Presqu'île parking is a large shaded parking lot overlooking the calanque ... costs €8 during high season ... located at 1 Avenue Plage Bleue, 13260 Cassis ... The Gorguettes parking lot ... free with 220 spaces, and a free shuttle then serves the center of Cassis and Port-Miou.

claim: From 1 June to 30 September 2026 massif access is governed daily by a prefectural fire-risk decision; on red/black days all trails close and the Route des Crêtes shuts, while only Sugiton (not En-Vau, Port-Miou or Port-Pin) requires a mandatory free reservation on set 2026 dates.
quote: Prohibition to access the Calanques massif (closure of all trails) ... Sugiton requires mandatory free reservation ... Weekends June 20-21 ... Daily June 27 - August 30 ... En-Vau and Cassis-side calanques (Port-Miou, Port-Pin) have NO mandatory reservation systems.

claim: Walking access depends on a prefectoral decision from 1 June to 30 September 2026; walking is usually allowed when wind is low and heat moderate, but any fire risk forbids entry.
quote: Walking regulations depends on a prefectoral decision ... if any risk of fire, the entrance is forbidden.
